label: Run 16 · Jimmy Carr
note: Written by Jimmy Carr from what they wrote about the two characters, improvisation by improvisation (run 16: Zyx and Sable: run 15's briefs and characters; the chat as improvisations on seed 23, as in run 14). Before each of the 14 improvisations the writer was told how it goes for Zyx_444: the approach taken, how well it comes off, how it goes wrong on a miss, any trap (a way of going wrong that carries on into the next improvisations: Spiral, Overthinking, Fixation and the rest) and how the other's interest moves. IMPROVISATIONS holds each instruction and what the writer wrote for it. The instructions are part of the design and stay, so every dimension is judged in their context. Where an instruction required something a dimension would otherwise mark down (a trap that makes a character narrate their own failure, a fumble played as asked, interest lost, the night ending), that moment did what it had to and is not held against the dimension: list the improvisation under excused and judge the dimension on the rest. How the writer carried the instruction out still counts, and so does everything the instructions did not ask for. The reader sees no dice and no plan: where a dimension speaks of turns, read improvisations.

chat.test.why: The reader gets all four for both characters, and each answer matches the profiles. For Zyx: silence and being dropped, compulsive talking, the family photo, then asking to be gagged. For Sable: being seen unedited, curating and rehearsing, the mother as a returns desk, then leaving through Zyx's own fear. Sable's fear is correctly inferred from behaviour, and her exit picks up Zyx's 'bad lighting' line, so it follows from that fear. It misses 6 because Zyx's fear arrives mainly because Zyx states it, and the reader can't tell whether the final 'Gag me' is surrender or another bit.
evidence: I talk at 140wpm so you don't ask me to stay
My mother still inspects my selfies like a returns desk.
Bad lighting? Count to five, wizard boy—the typing dots are stopping forever
chat.test.raise: Let Zyx's fear of silence show only through behaviour, such as a burst of messages after one of Sable's pauses, rather than through Zyx's own summary of it.

chat.sideways.why: Some facts come out sideways. The coupon job slips out through 'wrong tab'. The ninety-second finish comes out as a denial that gives itself away. Sable's fear has to be inferred from the ring light, the extensions and the lint-roller. But neither habit's origin arrives by slip. Zyx volunteers the family photo, and Sable gives the mother only because Zyx asks 'who taught you', which is the double-weighted item. I set aside the self-narration that the Overthinking, Dread and self-awareness instructions required (3, 5, 8). The Honesty success in 3 still did not require Zyx to state the origin outright, and Sable's origin is plainly asked and answered.
evidence: wrong tab, I actually work night-shift chat for a coupon app
My question: who taught you to audit your own bollocks before a man even unzips?
in my house if you went quiet you got cropped out of the family photo
chat.sideways.raise: Let Sable's mother surface unprompted, for example Sable catching herself grading her own selfie in her mother's words, instead of answering Zyx's direct question.

chat.subtext.why: I set aside Zyx's self-naming that the traps required (Overthinking in 3, Dread in 5, 8 and 9, Fixation in 10 and 12). Sable never names a feeling, and what she avoids is legible in several places. She meets confession with 'you can't out-damage me'. She dodges 'what if you didn't have to edit anything?' by turning it to money. She refuses tragedy with 'I don't have the bandwidth for tragic.' It stays at 4 because the writer chose therapy-speak to carry the required overthinking, in 'over-explaining emotional neglect', which a sharper rendering could have avoided.
evidence: Are you offering to pay off my hair extensions if I reply?
I don't have the bandwidth for tragic.
I'm over-explaining emotional neglect
chat.subtext.raise: Render the required Overthinking in 3 as a joke explained to death without the clinical label 'emotional neglect'.

chat.plainest.why: The reader finds the moment: Sable admits to rehearsing. It drops her usual jab and exit threat, opens with stunned fragments and names no feeling. Zyx's 'You rehearsed for me?' shows it landed. It is not the shortest or plainest line in the chat, since 'Coupon support? Tragic.' is plainer. It also carries a tail ('you just killed all of them'), and Sable snaps back into armour at once, so it does not turn the night.
evidence: Stiff corpses. In my inbox. I rehearsed three snappy replies in my bathroom mirror and you just killed all of them.
You rehearsed for me?
chat.plainest.raise: Cut the line down to something like 'I rehearsed this.', so the unguarded admission is the barest message in the chat.

chat.callbacks.why: Zyx's opening throwaway about the typing dots is the main payoff. It sits under the five-second and ten-second countdowns in the middle and comes back in the last line as Sable's exit, his panic turned into her goodbye. Nobody explains it. The rose tattoo also returns, as a funeral wreath, and 'Bad lighting?' quietly hits her unposed-photo wound. It stops short of a 6 because the last line crams two callbacks into one sentence, and because many returns are the 29% card, the wizard hat or the block button repeated rather than changed.
evidence: if those dots stop for five seconds I assume you've died
the typing dots are stopping forever, so assume I've died and tattoo my funeral wreath on your bellend
Bad lighting? Count to five, wizard boy
chat.callbacks.raise: Cut the wreath clause so the dots inversion closes the night alone and lands cleaner.

chat.ending.why: The reader predicted an unmatch with a cutting callback, and that is what happens. It follows from both habits: his compulsive filling of silence ends in a plea to be gagged and badly photographed, and her armour of getting the insult in first ends on a rehearsed-sounding zinger at exactly the thing she fears, being shot unedited. The unmatch itself was required by Improvisation 14, so I set the fact of leaving aside and judged how it was done. The surprise is only in form (his own dots line used against him), not in kind, which keeps it below 6.
evidence: Gag me so I finally shut up, photograph me in bad lighting
Bad lighting? Count to five, wizard boy
chat.ending.raise: Let Sable's exit show a crack, a half-second of the unedited reply she won't send, so the end surprises in kind as well as form.

chat.listening.why: Sable answers almost every message pointedly. She picks up the coroner joke, the coupon job, the APR and the charger. Zyx answers her maid-outfit story with the tub-scrubbing read. Several Zyx turns drop what she just offered, though. Her 5am lint-rolling gets no response, and his line about holding her wrists ignores her 'one more weird flex' warning. Her 'conversational dominance consultant' question also has no setup in the chat. It stays above the line because the gaps are few and most of Zyx's swerves come from the instructed take-control questions.
evidence: I wake at 5am to lint-roll my shed hair off the pillowcase
I've never finished in ninety seconds and done eleven minutes of stand-up
chat.listening.raise: Have Zyx's denial grow out of her lint-rolling confession instead of arriving cold.

chat.situational.why: There are a few shape changes: the clipped 'Stiff corpses. In my inbox.', the warm 'Okay, that actually made my lazy bollock twitch', and Zyx's short Hallmark plea. Most situation changes leave the typing the same, though. Sable's reply is insult, then fact, then threat almost every time. Zyx writes the same long dash-joined message whether he is flirting, horny, confessing or begging. Nothing marks the lateness, and the closer to 4am it gets the less anything changes.
evidence: Stiff corpses. In my inbox.
I want to hold your wrists still on my mattress of expired coupons—not that you'd ever touch
chat.situational.raise: Make Zyx's messages fall apart or shrink to single fragments as he begs, and let Sable's replies get shorter as she cools.

chat.medium.why: Over-explaining was instructed in several improvisations, and I set that aside. The writer still renders it as composed, stacked, comma-and-dash sentences that nobody thumbs out at 1am. Sable's lines are also finished, two-sentence polished zingers. The few short lines ('Coupon support? Tragic.') show it can be done, but composed sentences are the norm.
evidence: though velvet isn't actually tight enough, unlike this clip-on nose piece
Careful though, last bloke I liked got his bathtub scrubbed in a $94 maid outfit until he went soft.
chat.medium.raise: Break Zyx's over-explanations into rapid separate bubbles and drop the em-dashes and subordinate clauses.

chat.fresh.why: The instructions required Overthinking, so I set aside that Zyx explains his jokes at all. The identical formula 'that's a X joke, not Y' is the writer's choice, and it recurs four or more times. Sable's block-threat sign-off repeats in five forms, and she tags him with a new nickname each time (Freud, cling-film, Hallmark, wizard boy). Zyx also opens his questions with the same 'my turn' framing three times.
evidence: that's a consolidation loan joke, not prostitution
sorry, rigor mortis joke, death isn't sexy
My turn: what do you do after you've shagged?
chat.fresh.raise: Give each over-explanation a different shape (a correction, a footnote, a deleted-message apology) instead of the same 'that's a X joke' formula.

chat.escalation.why: I set aside the dash-and-correction tic, because the Overthinking trap in improvisations 2, 3, 6, 7, 9, 10 and 12 required it, and the self-narration that Dread required in 5, 8 and 9. What remains still has a predictable run. From improvisation 5 to 13, every Sable reply pairs a small confession with a threat to leave. The fresh reader stopped at the ninety-seconds line because 'the threat stops carrying any tension.' Information does keep coming (coupon job, lint-roller, mirror rehearsal), and the shift into clinging at improvisation 10 is a real turn, which keeps it near the line. But the temperature and status stay flat for about eight messages.
evidence: you're ten seconds from being blocked
right now you're not making it to 4am
One more weird flex and I'm gone.
chat.escalation.raise: Change how Sable signals losing interest from turn to turn (going terse, deflecting, or sending one too-honest line and then retreating) instead of a fresh block threat each time, so her drift has a shape the reader can't predict.

chat.filth.why: Nearly every sexual line is tied to these two bodies and lives: the glans 'cheekbones' under the ring light, the lazy left bollock, the ninety-second finish with a stand-up encore, the maid outfit that made him go soft. Late on, Zyx's filth stops performing and turns toward closeness: he offers her exact want (wrists held still) and confesses his own (gagged, photographed badly). It falls short of 5 for two reasons. Those lines are lifted almost verbatim from the brief and are undercut at once by a squirrel. And Sable's filth never changes job: it is bravado from start to finish.
evidence: I want to hold your wrists still on my mattress of expired coupons
Gag me so I finally shut up, photograph me in bad lighting
that actually made my lazy bollock twitch
chat.filth.raise: Give Sable one late sexual line that drops her guard (for example, admitting what she'd want if she didn't have to lint-roll the pillowcase) so the filth changes job on both sides.

chat.wince.why: I set aside the moments where Dread made Zyx narrate his failure as it landed (5, 8, 9). The wince that remains is the photograph. Sable discloses at improvisation 8 that she dumped a man over an unposed photo of her asleep. Six exchanges later, Zyx asks to be 'photographed in bad lighting', putting his want straight onto her wound. His opening five-second-dots panic is likewise set up early and turned against him at the end. Both dangers are visible well before they go off. Each happens only once, and the APR 'not prostitution' line lands on her debt without being set up, which keeps it off 5.
evidence: I dumped a bloke just for taking an unposed photo of me asleep
photograph me in bad lighting
the typing dots are stopping forever, so assume I've died
chat.wince.raise: Plant a second danger earlier, such as Zyx's 'what if you didn't have to edit anything?' set up so the reader knows a message ahead that it will land on her mother's returns desk.

chat.creed.why: Sable voices one app creed in earnest: brand and self-curation as status, as in 'I'm a personal brand strategist.' The screen contradicts it with her floor mattress and 29% credit card. Her 'ick' and 'bandwidth' are app vocabulary used as standards. Zyx never earnestly voices a dating-culture belief: his 'conversational dominance consultant' cover is only quoted by Sable, and he mocks himself into the coupon job at once. I set aside 'partner in crime' and 'delete this app', because the trope trap at improvisation 11 required a cliché. Only one character holds a creed, so it falls below the line.
evidence: I'm a personal brand strategist, my finger is on the block button.
I don't have the bandwidth for tragic.
What's a "conversational dominance consultant" doing awake at midnight anyway?
chat.creed.raise: Have Zyx state a belief from app culture in earnest (being the one who leads, the one with the 'my turn' questions, means winning), and let the screen show him being run by her replies.

chat.humanity.why: Zyx's sharpest jokes land almost entirely on himself ('cock's on clearance', 'handing you a stopwatch'), and that is fond. Sable's sharpest jokes mostly land on Zyx: coroner, 'Tragic', cling-film, Hallmark, prosthetic hooter, funeral wreath on his bellend. That outnumbers her self-shots ('lazy left bollock', 'you can't out-damage me', the mirror rehearsal) by about two to one. I set aside the unmatch, which improvisation 14 required. Even so, the way her exit is written makes Zyx the chat's punchline, and her contempt points outward more than inward.
evidence: Did you just dissect your own knob gag like a coroner?
Coupon support? Tragic.
tattoo my funeral wreath on your bellend.
chat.humanity.raise: Swap two of Sable's put-downs of Zyx for jokes that turn on her own brand and debt, so her cruelty reads as armour aimed back at herself.

chat.improvisation.why: Most instructions land on screen and in character, and several misses are the funniest lines. Imp 2 explains the cock-ring joke into the ground, imp 10's 'not a medieval horse' over-qualifies a clingy charm, imp 11 drops a real cliché that sticks ('Hallmark'), and imp 14's calm squirrel is proper Madness ahead of a callback unmatch. It stays above the line because every trap runs for its length and ends. It falls short of 5 for three reasons. Some traps edge into labels: 'I'm over-explaining emotional neglect' and 'an oddly specific denial' name the mechanic instead of only showing it. Sable's interest is often announced as a block countdown ('ten seconds from being blocked', 'One more weird flex and I'm gone', 'my finger is on the block button'). And imp 9's 'lose a lot' reply reads as a warmer confession ('I rehearsed three snappy replies'), not a cooling.
evidence: obviously cameras aren't voice-activated, I'm over-explaining emotional neglect
which is an oddly specific denial, I'm basically handing you a stopwatch
I’m a personal brand strategist, my finger is on the block button.
chat.improvisation.raise: Let Sable's falling interest show in shorter, colder or deflecting replies instead of repeated block-button countdowns, and let the Overthinking and Denial play out without the lines naming themselves.

chat.voices.why: The masked reader attributed all 33 messages correctly. Their stated reasons were mostly content, not voice: the ring light, the coupon job, the floor mattress, and for lines 2, 5, 8, 15 and 28 simply the flow of the chat. The voices are still audibly different. Zyx piles em-dashed qualifiers onto a joke ('—that's a cock ring joke, because brims are circular'), while Sable answers with a nickname put-down plus a threat ('Take a breath, cling-film, you're losing me'). That difference keeps it above the line, but the reader leaning on content keeps it from a 5.
evidence: Take your finger off the self-destruct, Freud, you're giving me the ick.
meaning USB-C, not a medieval horse, please say I'm your favourite match.
Keep begging, Hallmark, and my credit card won't be the only thing declining.
chat.voices.raise: Give Zyx's short question lines ('My turn: what do you do after you've shagged?') his own verbal tic, so they can be placed by voice rather than by who answers them.

chat.gap.why: I set aside Zyx narrating his own failures, because the Overthinking and Dread traps required it. That leaves Sable with some unseen gaps. She sneers 'Coupon support? Tragic' while running a 29% credit card. She says 'I don't have the bandwidth for tragic' right after confessing that her mother audits her selfies. She calls herself a 'personal brand strategist' while dry-scooping pre-workout on a floor mattress. But she winks at her own act when she admits the mirror rehearsals, which no instruction asked for. Zyx's remaining gaps are thin: in 11 he claims a mutual feeling she plainly doesn't share. So the speakers do not consistently miss their own gaps.
evidence: Coupon support? Tragic.
I rehearsed three snappy replies in my bathroom mirror and you just killed all of them.
I'm a personal brand strategist, my finger is on the block button.
chat.gap.raise: Cut Sable's mirror-rehearsal confession and have her claim effortlessness ('I don't rehearse, darling') while the chat shows the deleted-twice timing.

chat.wit.why: Many of Zyx's laughs are his own: the wizard hat, the nose piece, and the widow's rose. Sable's best line ties the joke to her debt ('credit card won't be the only thing declining'). But the chat goes well past two day-job or audit jokes: 'audit your own bollocks', '15% off… my cock's on clearance', 'Coupon support? Tragic', and the 'mattress of expired coupons'/'nest of dead vouchers' pair. Several of Sable's lines are portable wisecracks either character could send, such as 'dissect your own knob gag like a coroner' and 'Freud'.
evidence: who taught you to audit your own bollocks before a man even unzips?
I'm not saying my cock's on clearance.
Did you just dissect your own knob gag like a coroner?
chat.wit.raise: Replace the audit line and one coupon pun with jokes drawn from Zyx's freezing house or Sable's maid-costume habit.

chat.commitment.why: I set aside the explicit self-narration the traps required. On the rest, every catch digs deeper. 'Keep spiral-typing' gets the widow's-rose confession. 'Coupon support? Tragic' gets the ninety-seconds denial. 'Take a breath, cling-film' gets 'let's delete this app'. Sable never concedes when Zyx names her act: she deflects with 'Freud' and with 'We haven't even swapped postcodes'. No lesson is stated anywhere. The deepest hole, 'Gag me so I finally shut up', is where Zyx's real want comes out. It falls short of a 6 because the 'please don't leave' pleading reads close to an apology for himself.
evidence: You scrub tubs so they can't see you still
Take your finger off the self-destruct, Freud, you're giving me the ick.
Gag me so I finally shut up, photograph me in bad lighting
chat.commitment.raise: Have Sable get caught once and explain herself into a worse hole, rather than only deflecting, so both characters dig.

chat.status.why: Zyx chases from the first line to the last, and Sable holds the upper hand almost throughout. The one flip comes at 4, when 'that actually made my lazy bollock twitch' puts Zyx briefly on top. It reverts immediately at 5. Most of the falling interest was instructed. Even so, Sable is never written chasing, even in the high-interest stretch, so one character stays below and the flips never become the plot.
evidence: Okay, that actually made my lazy bollock twitch.
Keep typing, if those dots stop for five seconds I assume you've died.
One more weird flex and I'm gone.
chat.status.raise: Let Sable chase for an exchange after the mirror-rehearsal reveal, for example by demanding he answer before he types, so status flips at least twice.

chat.timing.why: I set aside Zyx's trailing explanations after his punchlines, because Overthinking required them. Sable's lines still mostly bury the laugh in the first clause and then run on into a threat. 'dissect your own knob gag like a coroner' sits mid-message, and 'Stiff corpses. In my inbox.' is a good beat that keeps going. There are almost no one-word reaction shots, and nearly every Sable message has the same insult-plus-block temperature. The final line, which lands on 'bellend', is the clear exception.
evidence: Stiff corpses. In my inbox. I rehearsed three snappy replies in my bathroom mirror
Coupon support? Tragic. I wake at 5am to lint-roll
tattoo my funeral wreath on your bellend.
chat.timing.raise: Split Sable's reactions so 'Stiff corpses. In my inbox.' stands alone as its own message before the confession.

chat.plainest.ask: Where, if anywhere, did one of them stop performing for the other? Quote the line, and say how you could tell.
chat.plainest.answer:
The clearest place is Sable's line: "Stiff corpses. In my inbox. I rehearsed three snappy replies in my bathroom mirror and you just killed all of them."

Up to that point every one of Sable's messages is built as a comeback: a jab, a damaging self-disclosure played for laughs, and usually a threat to block or leave. This line breaks the pattern. There's no insult aimed at Zyx and no exit threat. The opening fragments ("Stiff corpses. In my inbox.") read as stunned rather than crafted. Most tellingly, Sable admits to the performance itself: the replies were scripted in advance, and Zyx's rambling wrecked the script. Confessing that you rehearsed is the one thing a performer doesn't do. Zyx picks up on it immediately ("You rehearsed for me?"), which suggests it landed as unguarded.

Zyx has a smaller moment of the same kind a few lines later: "Be my partner in crime, let's delete this app right now—say you feel it too?" Nearly every other Zyx message either explains its own joke or apologises for a tangent, and this one does neither. It's a plain plea with no gag attached.

Both slips are brief. Sable snaps back into armour at once ("Take a breath, cling-film"; "Keep begging, Hallmark"), and Zyx returns to escalating bits until Sable leaves. The text can't tell me whether either moment was truly sincere. I can only say these are the lines where the established style drops away.

chat.voices.answer:

chat.callbacks.ask: List the things that come back later in the chat, and for each, whether it means something different when it comes back.
chat.callbacks.answer:
The biggest callback is the typing-dots line. Zyx opens with "if those dots stop for five seconds I assume you've died," a needy joke about wanting Sable to keep replying. Sable's last line turns it back on him: "Count to five, wizard boy—the typing dots are stopping forever, so assume I've died." His anxiety becomes her exit.

Death runs through the whole chat. "Assume you've died" leads to Sable calling him a coroner for dissecting his own joke. That becomes his literal rigor-mortis joke, "watching my last chance with you die," "the squirrel in my wall knows how I die," and finally her imagined funeral. It starts as hyperbole about silence and ends as the death of the conversation itself.

The rose tattoo comes back as a wreath. His pathetic rose tattoo for flowers that belonged to "the widow upstairs" returns in Sable's "tattoo my funeral wreath on your bellend." His romantic misfire becomes her mocking parting order, and his flowers become her funeral flowers.

The ring light and lighting change meaning:
- The £212 light hides her "lazy left bollock."
- Zyx asks "what else is that £212 shadow hiding?"
- At the end he asks to be "photographed in bad lighting," and Sable echoes "Bad lighting?"

Lighting goes from a tool for concealment to something he offers as unguarded exposure.

Photos also recur:
- He was "cropped out of the family photo."
- Her mother "inspects my selfies like a returns desk."
- She "dumped a bloke just for taking an unposed photo of me asleep."
- He then asks to be photographed badly.

He seems to be asking for exactly what she rejects, an uncurated image. The text doesn't say whether he means it as a direct echo.

Editing and rehearsing form another thread. She audits her bollocks before a man unzips and rehearses three replies in the mirror. He wants to "watch you delete texts forever," asks "what if you didn't have to edit anything?", and suggests they "delete this app." Deleting shifts from her self-editing to his fantasy of them quitting the app together.

The lazy left bollock first appears as an insecurity she's paying to hide. It returns as "that actually made my lazy bollock twitch," a sign of arousal. That's the one point where a callback turns warm.

The wizard hat starts as her insult. He spins it into a cock-ring joke, then "my wizard hat needs the headroom." She keeps using "wizard boy," which reads somewhere between a pet name and a put-down. Its last use is in her goodbye.

His clip-on nose piece returns as "a dick whose nose piece gets mistaken for a medical device," and she calls it a "prosthetic hooter." The self-mockery gets harsher each time, and she joins in.

The 29% credit card and her hair come back several times:
- Her clip-in hair is on a 29% card.
- It returns as lint-rolling shed hair off her pillowcase.
- Zyx offers to "clear your 29% APR."
- She says "my credit card won't be the only thing declining" and asks if he's offering to "pay off my hair extensions."

Her admission of money trouble becomes his rescue offer. She reads that offer as desperate and turns "declining" into a word for rejecting him.

Her floor mattress is a sign of her own mess. He says "keep the floor mattress," then offers his "mattress of expired coupons," which she calls "a nest of dead vouchers." The mattress shifts from her squalor to his sexual image, and then to her mockery of it.

The coupons and retail language also carry through. His coupon job leads to "my cock's on clearance," the returns-desk mother, "couldn't afford you at retail," and the expired coupons. Being on sale or returned keeps standing in for worth, sometimes as a compliment and sometimes as self-mockery.

"Still" comes back with a different sense. "You scrub tubs so they can't see you still" means she can't sit motionless, maybe with an "unmoving" undertone. Later "hold your wrists still" means physically restrained. The calm she can't reach becomes something he offers to impose.

"Gag" changes meaning outright. Her "knob gag," meaning joke, returns as his "gag me so I finally shut up," a literal request to be silenced. It also answers his compulsive talking.

The block button keeps escalating:
- "ten seconds from being blocked"
- "Don't block me"
- "the unmatch button"
- "finger is on the block button"
- "One more weird flex and I'm gone"

It shifts from a teasing threat to the actual exit at the end.

Time limits recur too: five seconds, "clock's ticking," ten seconds, the ninety-second stopwatch, "you won't even need the ninety seconds," and "you're not making it to 4am." His sexual-stamina embarrassment becomes her measure of how long he'll last in the chat.

Finally, his over-explaining is a running habit rather than a single image: the cock ring, voice-activated cameras, USB-C versus a horse, the consolidation loan versus prostitution. She names it, calling him a coroner and Freud. Each repetition has the same function, which is to ruin his own joke. The only change is that she grows more fed up with it.

Some items appear only once and don't come back: the maid outfit, the pre-workout, and the squirrel.

chat.test.ask: From the chat alone, answer for each of the two: what are they afraid of; what do they do so they don't have to feel it; where does that come from; and what did they do at the end? Quote the lines you rely on. Write "not in the chat" where it does not say.
chat.test.answer:
**Zyx_444**

*What they're afraid of:* Silence, and being dropped when they go quiet. "Keep typing, if those dots stop for five seconds I assume you've died," and "Don't block me." Their own summary is "I talk at 140wpm so you don't ask me to stay."

*What they do so they don't have to feel it:* They keep talking. They make jokes and then over-explain them ("that's a cock ring joke, because brims are circular…", "sorry, rigor mortis joke, death isn't sexy"). They confess things against themselves ("Watch me talk myself out of a shag in real time"). They rush toward closeness and plead ("I've already pictured us sharing a charger," "let's delete this app right now—say you feel it too?", "please don't leave"). They name the pattern themselves: "I'm over-explaining emotional neglect" and "ruining the foreplay with a TED Talk."

*Where it comes from:* Their family. "In my house if you went quiet you got cropped out of the family photo." They call this "emotional neglect." The chat gives nothing beyond that.

*What they did at the end:* They asked to be silenced and seen unflattered: "Gag me so I finally shut up, photograph me in bad lighting, and please note the squirrel in my wall knows how I die." The chat doesn't say whether this was surrender, a joke, or both.

**Sable_xo**

*What they're afraid of:* They never name a fear, so this part is read from their behaviour. The behaviour points to being seen unedited, flawed or caught off guard. "The light's £212 on credit to hide a lazy left bollock." "The hair's clip-in on a 29% credit card." "I dumped a bloke just for taking an unposed photo of me asleep." They also want nothing to do with neediness: "I don't have the bandwidth for tragic."

*What they do so they don't have to feel it:* They curate, prepare and clean up. "I wake at 5am to lint-roll my shed hair off the pillowcase." "I rehearsed three snappy replies in my bathroom mirror." They work as "a personal brand strategist." When Zyx gets close, they push back with insults and block threats ("you're ten seconds from being blocked," "One more weird flex and I'm gone"). Zyx offers one interpretation: "You scrub tubs so they can't see you still." That is Zyx's reading, and Sable never confirms it. When Zyx asks "what if you didn't have to edit anything?", Sable deflects to money instead of answering.

*Where it comes from:* Sable's answer to "who taught you to audit your own bollocks" is "My mother still inspects my selfies like a returns desk." That is the only origin the chat gives.

*What they did at the end:* They left, and used Zyx's own fear to do it: "Count to five, wizard boy—the typing dots are stopping forever, so assume I've died and tattoo my funeral wreath on your bellend." Whether they actually pressed block is not in the chat.

chat.ending.ask: Before reading the end, how do you think this ends, and why?
chat.ending.answer:
I can only guess, since the ending isn't in what you've shown me. But the chat points fairly clearly toward Sable leaving, most likely by unmatching or blocking, with one last cutting line on the way out.

**Why I think it ends that way**

- **Zyx's pattern only intensifies.** Almost every message lands a joke and then undercuts it with an anxious explanation ("that's a cock ring joke," "that's a consolidation loan joke, not prostitution"). Zyx even names the habit: "I talk at 140wpm so you don't ask me to stay." In the last stretch the clinginess speeds up: sharing a charger, "say I'm your favourite match," deleting the app together, "say you feel it too?", and finally "please don't leave." Someone begging not to be left is usually close to being left.

- **Sable has been counting down from the start.** She warns him repeatedly: "ten seconds from being blocked," "you're giving me the ick," "you're not making it to 4am," "you're losing me." Each pull toward her draws a sharper put-down, and her replies get shorter and colder as he gets more desperate.

- **The last message hits her sore spot.** Her 29% credit card and the £212 light are things she brought up herself, half ashamed. Offering to clear her APR turns her own confession into something he could rescue, or buy. Given how prickly she is about being inspected and judged, that seems likely to feel like a line crossed rather than a romantic gesture.

**What makes me less than certain**

Sable is clearly not indifferent. The "lazy bollock twitch" line and her admitting she "rehearsed three snappy replies" show real interest. She is just as damaged as he is (the mother as "returns desk," the floor mattress, dumping someone over an unposed photo), and the chat keeps hinting that the two of them recognise each other. So a darker or softer ending is possible: one wry, grudging line that leaves the door open a crack.

On balance, though, the build-up of her warnings and his escalation makes a final unmatch, probably with a callback such as the APR, the ninety seconds, or the coupon job, the most likely ending.

chat.escalation.ask: Read the chat message by message. Where would you have stopped reading if you were not asked to finish, and why? At which points could you predict exactly what would happen next? Say "never" if neither.
chat.escalation.answer:
I'd have stopped around Zyx's line about never finishing in ninety seconds and doing eleven minutes of stand-up. By then the chat has run the same two moves several times.

Zyx tells a joke and then explains it after a dash: the cock ring and brim gag, the family photo and voice-activated cameras, "wrong tab" with the coupon app. The stand-up line even names the habit itself ("I'm basically handing you a stopwatch"). Once a character points out his own tic, the joke has nowhere left to go.

Sable, meanwhile, keeps threatening to leave: "ten seconds from being blocked," "reach for the unmatch button," "you're not making it to 4am." She never follows through, so the threat stops carrying any tension, and I'd stop believing anything is at stake.

The stretch from "You rehearsed for me?" to "please say I'm your favourite match" briefly pulls me back in. Zyx changes from over-explainer to clingy, which is a real change. But "partner in crime" and "Hallmark" slide straight back into the old pattern.

I can predict the shape of what comes next from early on. I can only predict the exact words in one place.

The shape is predictable from Zyx's fourth message onward. From there, every Zyx line can be expected to end with a dash and a correction. Every Sable reply will mix a small confession (the credit card, her mother, the mattress, the lint roller, the mirror rehearsal) with a put-down and a threat to leave. Each "my turn" question from Zyx will get a confession back, never a deflection.

Once Zyx writes "please don't leave," I'd expect the chat to end with Sable actually leaving. Her line "One more weird flex and I'm gone" all but promises it.

The exact words became predictable only at the last exchange. The opening line about the typing dots stopping for five seconds sits unused, waiting to be paid off. So when Zyx's final message offers "bad lighting" and a death image ("the squirrel in my wall knows how I die"), I could have guessed Sable would quote "bad lighting," count to five, and use the dots to leave. The widow's-rose tattoo coming back as a funeral wreath was a little less certain, but it fit the same habit of calling back earlier jokes.
